verses.text: The church in Antioch had several prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius from Cyrene, Manaen, who had grown up with Herod the ruler, and Saul.
As they worshiped the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, “Set Barnabas and Saul apart for me for the work I’ve called them to do.”
After fasting and praying, they laid their hands on the two men and sent them off.
Sent out by the Holy Spirit, Barnabas and Saul went down to Seleucia and sailed from there to Cyprus.
In Salamis they announced God’s word in the Jewish synagogues. John was with them as their assistant.
They traveled across the island as far as Paphos, where they met a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet named Bar-Jesus.
He was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. The proconsul summoned Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear God’s word.
But Elymas the sorcerer—that is what his name means—opposed them and tried to turn the proconsul away from the faith.
Then Saul, also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, stared directly at him
and said, “You are full of deceit and every kind of trickery, child of the devil and enemy of everything right! Will you never stop twisting the Lord’s straight paths?
“Now the Lord’s hand is against you. You will be blind for a while and won’t see the sun.” At once a mist and darkness came over him, and he went around looking for someone to guide him by the hand.
When the proconsul saw what happened, he believed. He was amazed at the Lord’s teaching.
Paul and his companions sailed from Paphos to Perga in Pamphylia. John left them there and returned to Jerusalem.
They traveled on from Perga and came to Antioch in Pisidia. On the Sabbath they went into the synagogue and sat down.
After the readings from the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue leaders sent them this message: “Brothers, if you have something encouraging for the people, please speak.”
Paul stood up, motioned with his hand, and said, “People of Israel and everyone here who honors God, listen.
“The God of Israel chose our ancestors and made our people numerous while they lived as foreigners in Egypt. Then he brought them out of Egypt with mighty power.
“For about forty years in the wilderness, he was patient with them.
“After overthrowing seven nations in Canaan, he gave our people their land as an inheritance for about 450 years.
“After that, God gave them judges until Samuel the prophet.
“Then they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin, who ruled for forty years.
“After removing Saul, God raised up David as their king. God testified about him: ‘I have found David, Jesse’s son, a man whose heart follows mine. He will do everything I want.’
“From David’s descendants, God brought Israel a Savior, Jesus, as he had promised.
“Before Jesus came, John had already preached a baptism calling all Israel to turn back to God.
“As John finished his work, he said, ‘Who do you think I am? I’m not the one. Look, someone is coming after me, and I’m not worthy even to untie his sandals.’
“Brothers, descendants of Abraham, and all of you who honor God, this message of salvation has been sent to us.
“The people of Jerusalem and their rulers didn’t recognize Jesus or understand the prophets read every Sabbath. Yet by condemning him, they fulfilled what the prophets had said.
“They found no reason to put him to death, but still asked Pilate to have him killed.
“After they carried out everything written about him, they took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb.
“But God raised him from the dead.
“For many days he appeared to those who had traveled with him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are now his witnesses to the people.
“We bring you the Good News: God has fulfilled for us, their descendants, the promise he made to our ancestors.
“God fulfilled it by raising Jesus, just as the second psalm says: ‘You are my Son; today I have become your Father.’
“God raised him from the dead so that he would never decay again. He said, ‘I will give you the holy and faithful promises I made to David.’
“That’s why another psalm says, ‘You will not let your Holy One decay.’
“David served God’s purpose during his own generation, then died, was buried with his ancestors, and decayed.
“But the one God raised did not decay.
“So, brothers and sisters, know this: through Jesus forgiveness of sins is announced to you.
“Everyone who believes is made right through him in a way the Law of Moses could never accomplish.
“Be careful, then, or what the prophets spoke about may happen to you:
“‘Look, you who scoff! Be amazed and perish. I am doing something in your days that you would never believe, even if someone explained it to you.’”
As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the Gentiles begged them to share these words again the next Sabbath.
When the gathering ended, many Jews and devout converts followed Paul and Barnabas. The two spoke with them and urged them to keep living in God’s grace.
The next Sabbath, almost the whole city gathered to hear the Lord’s word.
When the Jews saw the crowds, jealousy took over. They opposed Paul’s words and insulted him.
Paul and Barnabas spoke boldly: “God’s word had to be spoken to you first. Since you reject it and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, we are turning to the Gentiles.
“For this is what the Lord commanded us: ‘I have made you a light for the nations, to bring salvation to the ends of the earth.’”
When the Gentiles heard this, they were glad and praised the Lord’s word. All who were appointed for eternal life believed.
The Lord’s message spread throughout the whole region.
But the Jews stirred up devout and influential women, along with the city’s leading men. They launched persecution against Paul and Barnabas and drove them out of the region.
They shook the dust from their feet against them and went to Iconium.
The disciples were filled with joy and the Holy Spirit.
